newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Institute sees stagnation of Yugo industry in 97.
newsitem.headline: Institute sees stagnation of Yugo industry in 97.

text.p: Lack of funds, low domestic demand and delayed reforms are key factors limiting Yugoslav industry output growth which has been sliding since last November, a Belgrade economic think-tank said on Wednesday.

"Prices completely stabilised in April but what is worrying is that industrial production was suddenly halted too," said Stojan Stamenkovic, leading economist of the Institute of Economic Sciences (IEN).
"We expect stagnation of industrial production", he said presenting the IEN's monthly report.

According to official statistics, retail prices in April rose only 0.1 percent against the previous month. In March industry output rose 7.4 percent against February or up 9.2 percent over March last year.

But according to seasonally adjusted data, March output fell 4.9 percent on February, IEN said. "It is only half of the expected growth for March considering calender and seasonal factors," said Stamenkovic.

After last year's upward May-October trend when industry output rose by 13.6 percent, industrial production continued its decline and fell by 3.5 percent between last November and March this year, IEN's report said.
Trade deficit in March remained $113 millions in February. Exports rose to $151 million from $139 million in February and imports stood at $264 million, up from $252 million in the previous month.
According to IEN, imports are growing now at a moderate monthly rate of 0.2 percent. On the other hand, exports are declining at a monthly rate of 3.3 percent.
